text:
Give Mira a heads-up before you leave, not a surprise. At 26 months, big feelings still outpace the words to handle them, so an abrupt exit tips her over.

A couple of things that help, per the Child Development & Wellbeing Companion's guidance on toddler transitions:

- A five- and two-minute warning ("two more slides, then shoes").
- A small closing ritual — wave bye to the swings, count steps to the gate.
- Let her make one small choice on the way out (which hand to hold, carry the water bottle) — it gives her a sense of control.

These usually ease up as she gets more practice with transitions, not overnight, but noticeably over a few weeks.
